strings.method.heading: How scores work
strings.method.lead: A package matters to the MoonBit ecosystem when other packages build on it. The score measures that reliance from the public registry, the way a journal impact factor measures how often a journal is cited.
strings.method.signals.title: Three signals
strings.method.signals.body: Every package gets a score S from three counts and the age of its latest release t:
strings.method.signals.dependents: Dependents: packages whose latest release declares this package as a dependency
strings.method.signals.recent: New dependents: those whose dependency first appeared in the last 180 days
strings.method.signals.log: The logarithm gives diminishing returns: going from 10 to 21 dependents adds as many points as going from 1000 to 2001. Dependents weigh most because a dependency is a deliberate decision; downloads also count automated builds.
strings.method.owners.title: Dependents of the same owner
strings.method.owners.body: An author who splits one project into many packages adds a dependent for every package. Such dependents count a quarter each, as citation indicators discount self-citations, so a package ranks high only when other people build on it. The package page shows both counts.
strings.method.recency.title: Release recency
strings.method.recency.body: The sum is multiplied by m(t): 1.12 for a release in the last 30 days, falling linearly to 0.88 at one year, and 0.88 after that. Maintained packages rank a little higher; an old package with many dependents still ranks high.
strings.method.grades.title: Grades
strings.method.grades.body: Grades place a package within the registry rather than on an absolute scale, like journal quartiles. Packages are sorted by score and cut at fixed shares; equal scores share a position.
strings.method.momentum.title: Momentum
strings.method.momentum.body: The score is computed again as it would have been 30 days ago, from the releases and dependencies published by then. A change counts only when it is at least 10 points and at least 10% of the earlier score, so neither a large package nor a tiny one changes label on noise.
strings.method.data.title: Data and updates
strings.method.data.body: The rankings are rebuilt every day from the mooncakes.io registry index and its download counts. Yanked releases are ignored, and only the dependencies of each package's latest release count.
strings.method.data.current: This snapshot was computed on {date} and ranks {count} packages.
strings.method.limits.title: What the score does not say
strings.method.limits.body: The score measures reliance, not quality. A young, excellent package can rank low, and a widely used one can still have bugs. Read the package page, its repository and its documentation before you depend on it.
strings.method.design: The full derivation in the score design notes
strings.momentum.rule: A change counts as rising or cooling only when it reaches both 10 points and 10% of the earlier score.
